item.title: Legacy Media Downplays Christian Persecution In Nigeria After Trump Admin Strikes
item.description: Legacy media outlets downplayed Christian persecution in Nigeria after President Donald Trump's administration struck anti-Christian ISIS terrorists in the country.

item.title: Is Ukraine Peace Deal Doomed Before Zelenskyy And Trump Even Meet At Mar-A-Lago?
item.description: As Ukraine and the U.S. try one more time to reach agreement on terms for a peace deal to end the war with Russia, questions remain about whether a resolution is still possible after multiple stalled rounds of negotiations.

item.title: Karoline Leavitt Announces Major Life News
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt announced on Friday that she is expecting her second child in the spring of 2026.

item.title: Trump-Backed Candidate Tito Asfura Wins Honduras Presidential Election
item.description: Honduras’ election authorities declared right-wing candidate Nasry "Tito" Asfura victorious in the country's presidential election on Wednesday.

item.title: Employees At DC’s Newest Gay Bar Get Fussy Over Unpaid Wages
item.description: Ex-employees at the Rush Bar and Lounge, a gay bar that launched in Washington, D.C. earlier this month, are having a big tiff with their boss after they said he did not pay them.

item.title: TAYLOR HAYNES: America’s Small Farmers Can Compete If We Let Them
item.description: The President’s new $12 billion bridge payment plan offers welcome short-term help for domestic farmers, but it also underscores how fragile the American agricultural economy has become – and how urgently we need reforms that outlast any single administration.

item.description: Deputies responding to the scene found Crystal dead inside the home. Her 13-year-old daughter had been shot in the face and shoulder but was still alive.

item.title: Tiny Pacific Island Featured on ‘Survivor’ Agrees to Take US Deportees for $7.5 Million
item.description: Under the deal, deportees whose home countries refuse to take them back — including nations such as China, Cuba, Russia, or Iran — would be allowed to live and work in Palau.

item.title: Snowstorm Grounds Holiday Travelers at JFK
item.description: By Friday evening, JFK had logged 158 canceled flights and 204 delays — the highest total of any airport in the country that day.
